bottleneck: Clinical sequencing returns variants of uncertain significance (VUS) far more often than clear diagnoses: a missense change in a disease gene may be pathogenic or benign, and functional evidence is missing for most of the millions of observed variants. Reclassification happens slowly and inconsistently across labs, leaving patients with genetic findings nobody can act on. Non-coding and structural variants are even harder to interpret, and each genome sequenced adds more VUS than it resolves.
current_state: Databases like ClinVar grow, and AI predictors improve, but the VUS rate remains high. Functional assays cannot keep pace with the flood of novel variants from expanding sequencing.

title: Variants of uncertain significance paralyze genomic medicine
why_it_blocks: Sequencing without interpretation is noise. Until VUS resolution keeps up with variant discovery, genomic medicine delivers anxiety as often as answers, and clinicians learn to distrust the reports they receive.
